spec_match.rationale: The API surface was read from WHATWG HTML PR 12590 rather than guessed: document.spellCheckCustomDictionary, [SecureContext], [SameObject], addWords(sequence<DOMString>), removeWords(sequence<DOMString>), no reader, case-sensitive matching. The probe checks each of those individually, including the absence of any read-back method, which is a requirement rather than a gap.

interactive.rationale: A live surface probe with a free-text property expression and three competing feature detections; a working editor with real spell checking, an editable glossary, a journal of the exact calls made or withheld, and a checkbox that really turns spellcheck off; and three live documents whose identities are counted and whose frame can be navigated to show a new one.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index describes the problem the feature solves — an application's own vocabulary underlined as misspellings, with spellcheck="false" as the only escape — which is the proposal's motivation, and says up front that these pages probe rather than demonstrate.

edge_cases.rationale: The non-secure-context case is measured and would be reported as the cause of an absent attribute; the write-only design is tested by looking for readers rather than assumed; the single-page-application trap (a document that is never replaced, so the dictionary never resets) is called out; and case-sensitivity is counted against the real text in the editor.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/6185007701557248 on the index and all three concept pages, with the WHATWG pull request, the HTML spelling-and-grammar section and MDN's spellcheck attribute.

conformance.rationale: Seven immutable assertions: the attribute exists (the feature), both methods exist, no read-back method exists, [SameObject] identity holds, addWords accepts a real glossary without throwing, the page is a secure context so an absent attribute is the browser's doing, and the spellcheck attribute — the workaround being replaced — still reflects per element.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150: 3/3, 25 assertions. Measured: the attribute is absent, both with and without --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, on a page that IS a secure context (localhost); the editor journalled the exact addWords and removeWords calls it would have made with real arguments; the spellcheck=false fallback really disables checking on the field; and navigating a frame moved it from doc#2 to doc#4, a new document object.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with whether the attribute is present, how many members were found, and how many distinct documents were counted.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, no raw colour literals, buttons set background and colour, 44px minimums on the main controls (the per-term remove buttons are deliberately small chips inside a 44px row), and every wide table in its own scroll container.

accessibility.rationale: Each glossary chip's remove button carries an aria-label naming the term it removes; the journal is role=log with a name; the fallback checkbox sits in a 44px label row; every result is announced through aria-live; the frames carry titles describing what they are.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Frame and fact grids are auto-fit minmax and stack at 360px; the glossary chips wrap; the textarea is width:100% with box-sizing; the wide tables scroll inside their own containers.

openQuestions.title: Nothing here can observe a spell-check result, and that will still be true when the API ships
openQuestions.detail: The editor page can add words and cannot verify the effect, because spell-check decisions are not exposed to script. That is by design and the page says so, but it means the demo will never be able to assert that a term stopped being underlined — the strongest evidence available will always be a screenshot or a reader's own eyes. Worth deciding whether a captured screenshot comparison belongs in the evidence for this feature when it lands.

openQuestions.title: Check the attribute name against the shipped implementation
openQuestions.detail: The proposal moved from window.spellCheckDictionary to document.spellCheckCustomDictionary during review, and the pages use the later name throughout. If Chrome ships a different spelling, the probes will report absent for the wrong reason — so the first run against a browser that has it should confirm the name rather than trusting the probe's silence.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible editable text field with spell checking and helper controls
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Label every field, keep helper controls reachable, and do not rely on a control's visual state alone to convey what it does.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The editor's textarea is labelled, the glossary chips carry per-term aria-labels on their remove buttons, and the spellcheck toggle is a real checkbox in a 44px label row whose effect is described in a live region rather than only visible in the field.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive toggles the checkbox and asserts both the field's spellcheck property and the announced text.

guidanceConsulted.query: announce the result of an action that cannot be verified
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Say what happened, including when nothing did; do not leave a control that silently fails looking as though it succeeded.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Every call is journalled with a marker for whether it was actually made, and the live region states plainly that the browser has no such attribute. Nothing on the page changes appearance as if the call had worked.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: The journal recorded '✗ would have called: …addWords([…])' with the real arguments.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive chip list and comparison cards without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Let chip lists wrap; auto-fit grids for cards; wide tables in their own scroll container.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The glossary is a wrapping flex list, the document cards are auto-fit minmax(250px), and all four tables sit in overflow-x:auto wrappers.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: responsive-check desktop + mobile on the feature.

summary: Three concepts for an API that is not here yet, built so that everything except the one unavailable call is real: real spell checking, a real glossary, real documents counted and replaced, and a journal that records the exact call with its exact arguments and says plainly that it did not happen.
